text:
Mike Greene: Quick check — we're provisioning an internal NLB in a customer VPC that will forward to a private service and then out to a 3rd-party log collector. Do we need an explicit egress IP allowlist on our side for the collector, and any redaction requirements for logs we push? Anyone from sec available?

Olivia Kim: A few clarifying q's: is this an internal (not internet-facing) NLB? What ports/protocols (TCP 443 only?) and are you preserving client source IPs or SNATing via NAT? If source IPs preserved, collector will see private ENI IPs.

Mike Greene: Yes internal NLB, TCP 443 only. We plan to avoid NAT; backend ENIs should preserve client IPs. Proposed security group / route snippet:```# SG for service
Inbound:
  - Type: TLS(443)
  - Source: sg-0a1b2c3d (internal app tier)
Outbound:
  - Type: TLS(443)
  - Destination: 3.45.67.89/32, 3.45.67.90/32  # partner collector
# route table: point default route to VPC endpoint ENI for collector
```Also planning a VPCE to S3 for log delivery with a restrictive endpoint policy.

Alex Patel: If the collector is third-party we require: 1) an allowlist of collector IPs posted to the infra ticket, 2) a short privacy review (logs may contain sourceIp and hostnames), and 3) an access approval from security. For logs: redact/mask private IPs and internal hostnames before sending (mask pattern for sourceIp and host like "10.*" or hostnames matching internal domains). See logging policy: https://redwood.company/policies/logging (summarized: no plaintext internal IPs in exported logs).

Sara Li: FYI from infra: we won't use NAT; VPCE + interface ENIs will be used for outbound to the collector. We'll add an S3 VPCE policy to limit PutObject to the designated bucket and only from the service role. Question on endpoint policy: do you want cross-account access blocked (yes we should block it unless explicitly allowed).

security-bot: Reminder: Please file an access review in the security queue for any external collectors. Per process, we need business justification, IP allowlist, retention policy, and the log redaction regex. Review due in 7 days.

Olivia Kim: Next steps: I'll add the SG + VPCE policy snippet to the infra PR and tag @Alex Patel for security signoff. @Mike Greene please open an infra ticket with partner IPs, business justification, and sample logs showing redaction.

Mike Greene: On it — partner IPs are 3.45.67.89/32 and 3.45.67.90/32. I'll attach example logs and proposed redaction regex (e.g., replace /\b10\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+\b/ with "<REDACTED_IP>"). Thanks :thumbsup:
